note: Every backend/src/**/*.ts arithmetic site this ratchet finds outside the four eslint-scoped modules (src/intakes/, src/payouts/, src/shifts/, src/supplier-balance/) and outside *.spec.ts/*.db-spec.ts, as of 2026-09-10: 29 keys, 32 occurrences. Read individually before writing a reason, not inferred from the shape of the code. Four of the 29 keys are backend/src/common/money.ts's OWN internals (the *, /, and mul()'s two / occurrences on one line) — the money engine works in bigint, not JS number, so it carries none of the float-precision risk this ratchet exists to catch, but the AST heuristic only recognises number-typed or numeric-literal operands, not bigint-safety, so those sites are listed honestly here rather than exempted by widening the rule's path exclusions. Two keys (backend/src/seed/dev-seed.ts:52 and :59) are a genuine concern flagged in this task's report, not a false positive: the dev seed script reimplements money.ts's add() independently, through Number() and plain-number division, to compute real values written into grade_prices.base_price for the seeded demo dataset — a real duplicate of the one authorised rounding seam, left as-is because backend/src is out of scope for this task. Two keys (password-hashing.ts:28's two occurrences) are literal-and-number-typed arithmetic that this rule's single-level operand check cannot prove clear because each is the OUTER multiplication of a left-associative a*b*c chain, whose left operand is itself a BinaryExpression rather than a bare literal or identifier. Every remaining key is one of two shapes: the repeated (page - 1) * limit pagination-offset arithmetic this template's list endpoints all share (10 keys, including pagination-query.dto.ts's own skipOf() helper), or an env-var/config integer parsed with Number()/parseInt() (ports, throttle window/limit) or Math.min() retry-backoff arithmetic that is never a monetary or weight value. None were left unclassified — every entry's reason states what the arithmetic actually is, read at its site. This ratchet is two-directional: a new site not listed here fails scripts/verify/ratchets/money-rounding.mjs, and a listed entry whose site (or exact occurrence count) no longer matches the tree fails it too — this file may only shrink or be re-dated by a reviewed change, never grow by drift.

money.ts's own parse(): BigInt(whole) * UNIT, scaling the integer part of a decimal string up to kopiykas. This is the one seam §5.1 authorises to take a numeric string apart; it works in bigint, not JS number, so it carries none of the float-precision risk this ratchet exists to catch — but the AST heuristic only recognises number-typed/numeric-literal operands, not bigint-safety, so it is listed honestly here rather than exempted by path.

money.ts's own format(): magnitude / UNIT, recovering the whole-kopiyka part from the internal bigint representation before rendering it back to a decimal string. Same seam, same bigint-not-number reasoning as line 43 above.

money.ts's own mul(): parse(a) * parse(b), the scale-4 bigint product before mul() rounds it back to scale 2 half-up. This IS the rounding engine itself — §2.7's amount calculation runs through exactly this line — audited by money.spec.ts, not by this AST heuristic.

money.ts's own mul(): (magnitude + UNIT / 2n) / UNIT implements half-up-away-from-zero rounding on the bigint product; the two / occurrences on this one line are the inner UNIT / 2n and the outer division by UNIT. Same seam as lines 43/51/75 — bigint arithmetic implementing the one authorised rounding rule, not a bypass of it.

toCents()'s own body: Number(whole) and Number(frac.padEnd(2, '0')) — converts a decimal string's parsed integer and fractional parts to JS numbers before summing as cents. It is confined to the dev seed script (never a runtime dependency of the app — see the seam check) and today's seed prices are small enough that no precision loss surfaces in practice, but it is a real duplicate of money.ts's add(), not a provably-safe pattern, so it is listed rather than exempted.

maxmemFor()'s own body: Math.max(32 * 1024 * 1024, 256 * n * r) computes scrypt's maxmem option in bytes from the cost parameters N and r. Each inner multiplication (32 * 1024, 256 * n) clears on its own since every operand is a number-typed identifier or a numeric literal, but this rule inspects only a BinaryExpression's two immediate operands, so the OUTER multiplication in each left-associative chain ((32 * 1024) * 1024 and (256 * n) * r) sees a nested BinaryExpression as its left operand and is not provably cleared by this single-level heuristic. This is scrypt memory sizing, not money or weight.
const n = Number(rawN) — parses the scrypt cost parameter N back out of the self-describing stored-hash format (scrypt$N$r$p$salt$hash); a cost parameter, not money.
const r = Number(rawR) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter r; not money.
const p = Number(rawP) — same stored-hash format, the scrypt cost parameter p; not money.
